passages.text: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples), He left Judea and returned to Galilee.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus gained many disciples.
Jesus’ disciples baptized people.
Jesus Himself did not baptize.
The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John.
Jesus realized that the Pharisees knew this.
Jesus left Judea.
Jesus went back to Galilee.
passages.original: Ὡς οὖν ἔγνω ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὅτι Ἰησοῦς πλείονας μαθητὰς ποιεῖ καὶ βαπτίζει ἢ Ἰωάννης καίτοιγε Ἰησοῦς αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβάπτιζεν ἀλλ’ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀφῆκεν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν

passages.text: Now He had to pass through Samaria.
passages.sermon: Jesus was traveling from Judea to Galilee.\r\nHe needed to go through Samaria.
passages.original: Ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρείας

passages.text: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
passages.sermon:
Jesus traveled through Samaria.
He came to a town called Sychar.
Sychar was in Samaria.
This town was near a piece of land.
Jacob had given this land to his son Joseph.
passages.original: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας λεγομένην Συχὰρ πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ τῷ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
passages.sermon:
Jacob’s well was there.
Jesus was traveling.
Jesus became tired from His journey.
Jesus sat down by the well.
It was about the sixth hour.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ ὥρα ἦν ὡς ἕκτη

passages.text: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”
passages.sermon:
A woman from Samaria came to draw water.
Jesus saw the Samaritan woman.
Jesus spoke to her.
Jesus said, “Give Me a drink.”
passages.original: Ἔρχεται γυνὴ ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρείας ἀντλῆσαι ὕδωρ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δός μοι πεῖν

passages.text: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)
passages.sermon:
Jesus had disciples.
His disciples left.
They went into the town.
They went to buy food.
passages.original: οἱ γὰρ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεληλύθεισαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἵνα τροφὰς ἀγοράσωσιν

passages.text: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)
passages.sermon:
A Samaritan woman spoke to Jesus.
She said, “You are a Jew.”
She said, “I am a Samaritan woman.”
She asked, “How can you ask me for a drink?”
Jews do not associate with Samaritans.
passages.original: Λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρῖτις Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρ’ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς γυναικὸς Σαμαρίτιδος οὔσης οὐ γὰρ συνχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρίταις

passages.text: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Samaritan woman.
Jesus was a Jew.
He asked her for a drink.
He said, “If you knew the gift of God, you would understand.
If you knew who is speaking to you, you would ask Him for a drink.
He would give you living water.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι Δός μοι πεῖν σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν

passages.text: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?
passages.sermon:
A Samaritan woman spoke to Jesus.
She called Him “Sir.”
She said, “You have nothing to draw water with.”
She said, “The well is deep.”
She asked, “Where will You get this living water?”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Κύριε οὔτε ἄντλημα ἔχεις καὶ τὸ φρέαρ ἐστὶν βαθύ πόθεν οὖν ἔχεις τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν

passages.text: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”
passages.sermon:
The woman spoke to Jesus.
She asked Jesus a question.
She said, “Our ancestor is Jacob.
Jacob gave us this well.
Jacob drank from this well.
His sons also drank from this well.
His livestock drank from this well too.
Are you greater than Jacob?”
passages.original: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰακώβ ὃς ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ φρέαρ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔπιεν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ θρέμματα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the woman.\r\nHe said, “Everyone who drinks this water will become thirsty again.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Πᾶς ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος τούτου διψήσει πάλιν

passages.text: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman at the well.
Jesus offered her living water.
Anyone who drinks the water Jesus gives will never be thirsty again.
The water Jesus gives becomes a spring inside that person.
This spring of water rises up to eternal life.
passages.original: ὃς δ’ ἂν πίῃ ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος οὗ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ οὐ μὴ διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀλλὰ τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ δώσω αὐτῷ γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Sir, give me this water.
Then I will not be thirsty.
Then I will not have to come here to draw water.”
passages.original: Λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνή Κύριε δός μοι τοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ ἵνα μὴ διψῶ μηδὲ διέρχωμαι ἐνθάδε ἀντλεῖν

passages.text: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He said, "Go."
He said, "Call your husband."
He said, "Come back here."
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ Ὕπαγε φώνησον τὸν ἄνδρα σου καὶ ἐλθὲ ἐνθάδε

passages.text: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman at a well.
The woman answered Jesus.
She said, "I have no husband."
Jesus replied to the woman.
He said, "You are correct to say you have no husband."
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ἡ γυνὴ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Οὐκ ἔχω ἄνδρα Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Καλῶς εἶπας ὅτι Ἄνδρα οὐκ ἔχω

passages.text: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman at the well.
He said, “You have had five husbands.
The man you have now is not your husband.
You have told the truth.”
passages.original: πέντε γὰρ ἄνδρας ἔσχες καὶ νῦν ὃν ἔχεις οὐκ ἔστιν σου ἀνήρ τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἴρηκας

passages.text: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.
passages.sermon: A woman spoke to Jesus.\r\nShe said, “Sir, I see that you are a prophet.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Κύριε θεωρῶ ὅτι προφήτης εἶ σύ

passages.text: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”
passages.sermon:
The Samaritan woman spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Our fathers worshiped on this mountain.
You Jews say people must worship in Jerusalem.
You say Jerusalem is the place to worship.”
passages.original: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου προσκυνεῖν δεῖ

passages.text: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
Jesus said, “Believe Me, woman.
A time is coming.
You will not worship the Father on this mountain.
You will not worship the Father in Jerusalem.
You will worship the Father somewhere else.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πίστευέ μοι γύναι ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ Πατρί

passages.text: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.
passages.sermon:
You are Samaritans.
You worship what you do not know.
We are Jews.
We worship what we know.
Salvation comes from the Jews.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν

passages.text: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said a special time is coming.
This time is already here now.
True worshipers will worship the Father.
They will worship the Father in spirit.
They will worship the Father in truth.
The Father looks for people like this.
The Father wants people who worship Him in spirit and in truth.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ Πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν

passages.text: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”
passages.sermon:
God is Spirit.
God does not have a physical body.
People who worship God must worship Him in spirit.
People who worship God must worship Him in truth.
passages.original: Πνεῦμα ὁ Θεός καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτὸν ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δεῖ προσκυνεῖν

passages.text: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to Jesus.
She said, “I know the Messiah is coming.”
People call the Messiah ‘Christ.’
When the Messiah comes, He will explain everything to us.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή Οἶδα ὅτι Μεσσίας ἔρχεται ὁ λεγόμενος Χριστός ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ἅπαντα

passages.text: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the woman.\r\nJesus said, “I am the Messiah.”\r\nJesus said, “I am the one speaking to you.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ λαλῶν σοι

passages.text: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was talking with a woman.
His disciples returned at that moment.
The disciples saw Jesus speaking with the woman.
The disciples felt surprised.
No disciple asked Jesus, “What do you want from her?”
No disciple asked Jesus, “Why are you talking with her?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν Τί ζητεῖς ἢ Τί λαλεῖς μετ’ αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people, “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke with Jesus at a well.
Jesus told her important things about her life.
The woman left her water jar at the well.
She went back into the town.
She spoke to the people in the town.
She said, “Come and see a man who told me everything I ever did.”
She asked, “Could this man be the Christ?”
passages.original: Ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέν μοι πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησα μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.
passages.sermon: The people left the town.\r\nThey walked toward Jesus.
passages.original: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν

passages.text: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with His disciples.
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They called Him “Rabbi.”
They urged Him to eat something.
passages.original: Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Ῥαββί φάγε

passages.text: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “I have food to eat.\r\nYou do not know about this food.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε

passages.text: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”
passages.sermon: The disciples spoke to each other.\r\nThey asked a question.\r\nThey said, “Did someone bring Him food?”
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν

passages.text: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus said, “My food is to do the will of the One who sent Me.\r\nMy food is also to finish His work.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ποιήσω τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον

passages.text: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest.’
But I tell you, look up.
Open your eyes.
Look at the fields.
The fields are already ripe for harvest.”
passages.original: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν ἤδη

passages.text: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
passages.sermon:
The reaper works in the field.
The reaper receives his wages.
The reaper gathers a crop.
This crop leads to eternal life.
The sower also works in the field.
The sower and the reaper both rejoice together.
passages.original: Ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων

passages.text: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He explained a truth about spiritual work.
He said, “One person sows the seed.
Another person reaps the harvest.
This saying is true in this situation.”
passages.original: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων

passages.text: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I sent you to reap a harvest.
You did not do the hard work for this harvest.
Other people did the hard work before you.
You have entered into the results of their labor.
You now gather what others have prepared.”
passages.original: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε

passages.text: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”
passages.sermon:
Many Samaritans lived in that town.
These Samaritans heard a woman speak about Jesus.
The woman gave her testimony about Jesus.
She said, “He told me everything I ever did.”
Because of her testimony, many Samaritans believed in Jesus.
passages.original: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαριτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα

passages.text: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.
passages.sermon: The Samaritans came to Jesus.\r\nThey asked Jesus to stay with them.\r\nJesus stayed with the Samaritans for two days.
passages.original: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρῖται ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας

passages.text: And many more believed because of His message.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Samaritans.
Many Samaritans listened to Jesus.
Many more Samaritans believed in Jesus.
They believed because of His message.
passages.original: Καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ

passages.text: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.”
passages.sermon:
The Samaritans spoke to the woman.
They said, “We do not believe only because of what you said.
We have heard Jesus ourselves.
We know this man is truly the Savior of the world.”
passages.original: τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ Σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου

passages.text: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus stayed in the town for two days.
After two days, Jesus left that place.
Jesus went to Galilee.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν

passages.text: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus is a prophet.
Jesus spoke about prophets.
Jesus said a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.
Jesus testified this truth Himself.
passages.original: αὐτὸς γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι προφήτης ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι τιμὴν οὐκ ἔχει

passages.text: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.
passages.sermon:
Jesus arrived in Galilee.
The people of Galilee welcomed Him.
They had seen what Jesus did in Jerusalem at the feast.
They had also gone to the feast in Jerusalem.
passages.original: ὅτε οὖν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἐδέξαντο αὐτὸν οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι πάντα ἑωρακότες ὅσα ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ καὶ αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν

passages.text: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.
passages.sermon:
Jesus returned to Cana in Galilee.
Jesus had turned water into wine in Cana.
A royal official lived in Capernaum.
The royal official had a son.
The son was sick in Capernaum.
passages.original: Ἦλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον Καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ

passages.text: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.
passages.sermon:
A royal official lived in Capernaum.
His son was very sick.
The son was about to die.
The official heard news about Jesus.
He heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee.
The official went to Jesus.
He begged Jesus to come down to Capernaum.
He asked Jesus to heal his son.
passages.original: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνήσκειν

passages.text: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the royal official.\r\nJesus said, “You people want to see signs and wonders.\r\nIf you do not see signs and wonders, you will not believe.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε

passages.text: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”
passages.sermon: A royal official spoke to Jesus.\r\nThe official said, “Sir, come down before my child dies.”
passages.original: Λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός Κύριε κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου

passages.text: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the official.
Jesus said, “Go.”
Jesus said, “Your son will live.”
The man believed what Jesus said.
The man left to go home.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πορεύου ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ Ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐπορεύετο

passages.text: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.
passages.sermon:
The official was traveling home.
He was still on the way.
His servants met him.
They brought news to him.
They said his boy was alive.
passages.original: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ ζῇ

passages.text: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour.”
passages.sermon: The man asked his servants about the time his son got better.\r\nThe servants answered him.\r\nThey said, “The fever left your son yesterday at the seventh hour.”
passages.original: Ἐπύθετο οὖν τὴν ὥραν παρ’ αὐτῶν ἐν ᾗ κομψότερον ἔσχεν εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐχθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην ἀφῆκεν αὐτὸν ὁ πυρετός

passages.text: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.
passages.sermon:
The father learned something important.
He learned it at a specific time.
Jesus had spoken to him earlier.
Jesus had said, “Your son will live.”
The father realized that his son became well at that same hour.
The father believed Jesus.
Everyone in his household also believed.
passages.original: Ἔγνω οὖν ὁ πατὴρ ὅτι ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐν ᾗ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ καὶ ἐπίστευσεν αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη

passages.text: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.
passages.sermon: Jesus came from Judea into Galilee.\r\nJesus performed a sign in Galilee.\r\nThis sign was the second sign Jesus performed after coming from Judea.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ πάλιν δεύτερον σημεῖον ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλθὼν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν
